person.description: Someone who uses or runs the system: a customer, an operator, another team.
person.label: Person

system.description: Something that delivers value to its users and is owned by one team: yours, or one you depend on.
system.label: Software System

container.description: Something that runs or stores data and is deployed on its own: a service, a worker, a mobile app, a serverless function.
container.label: Container

component.description: A part of a container behind a clear interface: a controller, a domain service, an adapter.
component.label: Component

database.description: A container that stores data. It never starts an interaction.
database.label: Database

webapp.description: A container that is a browser front end.
webapp.label: Web App

queue.description: A container that carries messages between other containers.
queue.label: Queue

group.description: A labelled boundary with no meaning of its own: a team, a layer, a deployment zone.
group.label: Group

domain.description: A part of the problem space, in the language of the business rather than of the software.
domain.label: Domain

entity.description: A thing the domain keeps track of and that has an identity over time: a reservation, an order, a payment.
entity.label: Entity

adr.description: An architecture decision record: the context of a decision, the decision itself, its consequences and the alternatives that were considered.
adr.label: ADR

steps.help: Name the decision in a few words, e.g. "Use PostgreSQL for order storage".
steps.title: Title & status

steps.help: What forces are at play — the problem, constraints and drivers that make a decision necessary now?
steps.title: Context

steps.help: What did you decide? State it actively: "We will …".
steps.title: Decision

steps.help: Which other options did you consider, and why were they rejected?
steps.title: Alternatives

steps.help: What becomes easier or harder? Include the downsides and the risks you accept.
steps.title: Consequences

steps.help: Which parts of the architecture must follow this decision?
steps.title: Affected elements

steps.help: Does this decision replace an earlier one? Leave empty if not.
steps.title: Supersedes

fitness-fn.description: An objective, preferably automated check that the architecture still has a property it was designed for.
fitness-fn.label: Fitness Function

properties.label: Metrics (one per line: test(file › title) passed, or metric{labels} <= value unit)

steps.help: Name the architectural characteristic this function protects, e.g. "Checkout p95 latency".
steps.title: Name & category

steps.help: How is the characteristic measured — a test, a metric, a static check?
steps.title: What it measures

steps.help: When does it pass? Give a concrete threshold, e.g. "p95 < 300 ms".
steps.title: Success criteria

steps.help: Which ADRs does this fitness function verify?
steps.title: Verified decisions

steps.help: Which elements does it check?
steps.title: Guarded elements

need.description: Raw input in the stakeholder's own words, kept verbatim: a brief, a user story, a note, a regulation.
need.label: Need

steps.help: A short name, e.g. "Checkout brief from Sales". Pick what kind of input it is.
steps.title: Name & kind

steps.help: Paste the input as-is — a brief, user story, notes or raw requirements. No format needed; Radical Forge or you can turn it into EARS requirements later.
steps.title: Text

steps.help: Who it came from or where it lives (a person, meeting, ticket or link).
steps.title: Source

steps.help: Is this part of a broader need, e.g. one stakeholder's notes within a discovery? Leave empty if not.
steps.title: Part of

requirement.description: One thing the system shall do, written as an EARS sentence.
requirement.label: Requirement

steps.help: A short name for the requirement, e.g. "Lock account after failed logins".
steps.title: Name

steps.help: Type the requirement as one sentence and press Enter — the EARS fields are filled for you. Or skip and fill them in the next step.
steps.title: Sentence

steps.help: Pick the EARS pattern; only the clauses it uses are shown.
steps.title: EARS fields

steps.help: Why is this requirement needed? Who asked for it?
steps.title: Rationale

steps.help: Which elements must satisfy this requirement?
steps.title: Satisfied by

steps.help: Is this a refinement of a broader requirement, or derived from a need?
steps.title: Derives from

steps.help: Which decisions or fitness functions follow from it?
steps.title: Traces to

scenario.description: An acceptance example in Gherkin: given a starting situation, when something happens, then the outcome.
scenario.label: Scenario

properties.label: Metrics (one per line: test(file › title) passed, or metric{labels} <= value unit)

steps.help: Name the behaviour, e.g. "Card payment declined".
steps.title: Name

steps.help: The starting state: who is involved and what is already true.
steps.title: Given

steps.help: The single action or event under test.
steps.title: When

steps.help: The observable outcome. Add And/But steps below if needed.
steps.title: Then

steps.help: Which requirements does this scenario verify?
steps.title: Verified requirements

blueprint.description: A curated reference architecture imported from the Concept Hub.
blueprint.label: Blueprint

mockup.description: One screen of the product, optionally with a low-fi wireframe.
mockup.label: Mockup

steps.help: Which screen is this, and what does the user do on it?
steps.title: Screen

steps.help: A Figma / Penpot link, if the design exists. You can generate a wireframe from the properties panel later.
steps.title: Design link

steps.help: Which requirements or scenarios does this screen show?
steps.title: Illustrates

steps.help: Which part of the system renders it?
steps.title: Presented by

state-machine.description: The lifecycle of one entity: the states it can be in and the transitions between them.
state-machine.label: State Machine

state.description: A situation the entity can be in.
state.label: State

pseudostate.description: A point a state machine passes through but never rests in: where it starts, a choice, a history.
pseudostate.label: Pseudostate

event.description: Something that happens and can trigger a transition.
event.label: Event

process.description: A procedure: the steps it is made of, what repeats and what is an alternative.
process.label: Process

step.description: One part of a process, itself made of steps or not.
step.label: Step

interacts.description: Any meaningful interaction: the source calls, uses, sends to or delivers to the target. The label says what happens, the technology how.
interacts.label: Interacts

realises.description: The software behind a domain or an entity: the bounded context that implements the domain, or the element that owns the entity's data.
realises.label: Realises

part-of.description: A part of an aggregate points to its root.
part-of.label: Part of

references.description: One aggregate refers to another by id.
references.label: References

depends-on.description: The source domain needs the target to do its work.
depends-on.label: Depends on

partnership.description: How the models of two domains meet, with a context-mapping pattern.
partnership.label: Partnership

constrains.description: The decision, check or requirement applies to the target element.
constrains.label: Constrains

supersedes.description: The newer decision replaces the older one.
supersedes.label: Supersedes

implements.description: A fitness function checks that a decision still holds; a C4 element runs a state machine.
implements.label: Implements

satisfies.description: The element is what makes the requirement true.
satisfies.label: Satisfies

derives.description: A requirement turns stakeholder input into a shall-statement or refines a broader requirement; a need sits inside a broader need.
derives.label: Derives from

traces-to.description: The decision the requirement led to, or the check that keeps it.
traces-to.label: Traces to

verifies.description: The scenario is the acceptance test of the requirement or state machine.
verifies.label: Verifies

illustrates.description: The screen shows the requirement being met, the step of the scenario, or what the user sees in the state.
illustrates.label: Illustrates

presented-by.description: The part of the architecture that renders the screen.
presented-by.label: Presented by

navigates-to.description: One step of a screen flow, with what triggers it.
navigates-to.label: Navigates to

transition.description: The machine moves from one state to another: on an event, under a guard, running actions.
transition.label: Transition

lifecycle-of.description: The machine is the lifecycle of that entity.
lifecycle-of.label: Lifecycle of

properties.label: On (for a state: entry, exit or do)

performed-by.description: The person or part of the architecture that does the step.
performed-by.label: Performed by

viewpoints.description: The people and software systems, and how they use each other (C4 level 1).
viewpoints.label: System context

viewpoints.description: The software systems with the containers, web apps, databases and queues inside them, the people who use them, and every relation between them (C4 level 2).
viewpoints.label: Containers

viewpoints.description: One software system with the containers, web apps, databases and queues inside it, and the people, systems and containers they are related to: a view per system (C4 level 2).
viewpoints.label: Containers of a system

viewpoints.description: The containers and web apps with the components inside them, the databases and queues they use, and every relation between them (C4 level 3).
viewpoints.label: Components

viewpoints.description: One container or web app with the components inside it, and the people, systems, containers and components they are related to: a view per container (C4 level 3).
viewpoints.label: Components of a container

viewpoints.description: A matrix of the containers, web apps, databases and queues: who uses whom, and where the cycles are.
viewpoints.label: Container dependencies

viewpoints.description: The domains and subdomains, and how they depend on and partner with each other.
viewpoints.label: Domain map

viewpoints.description: The entities and aggregates, what they are part of and what they reference.
viewpoints.label: Domain model

viewpoints.description: One domain with its subdomains and entities, and the entities of other domains they reference or are part of: a view per domain.
viewpoints.label: Entities of a domain

viewpoints.description: A table of domains, their entities, and the systems, containers and components that realise each.
viewpoints.label: Domain realisation

viewpoints.description: A table of needs, the requirements refined from each, and the scenarios that verify those.
viewpoints.label: Traceability

viewpoints.description: A table of requirements, the elements that satisfy each and the scenarios that verify it.
viewpoints.label: Requirement coverage

viewpoints.description: The requirements no scenario verifies or nothing satisfies yet.
viewpoints.label: Requirement gaps

viewpoints.description: A table of the systems, containers and components that satisfy requirements, each with its requirements and the scenarios that verify them.
viewpoints.label: Responsibilities

viewpoints.description: A document of the needs, the requirements refined from each, and the scenarios and screens for each requirement.
viewpoints.label: Specification

viewpoints.description: A table of ADRs, the fitness functions that check each and the elements it constrains.
viewpoints.label: Decisions

viewpoints.description: A document of the ADRs, the newest first, each with the decisions it supersedes.
viewpoints.label: Decision log

viewpoints.description: A table of the fitness functions by category, each with the decisions it checks and the elements it constrains.
viewpoints.label: Fitness functions

viewpoints.description: The screens and how users navigate from one to the next.
viewpoints.label: Screen flow

viewpoints.description: A table of the screens, each with the requirements and scenarios it illustrates and the elements that present it.
viewpoints.label: Screens

viewpoints.description: A table of the entities with a lifecycle, the state machine of each, and what implements and verifies it.
viewpoints.label: Entity lifecycles

viewpoints.description: One state machine with its states, pseudostates, events and transitions, and the entity it is the lifecycle of: a view per machine.
viewpoints.label: State machine

viewpoints.description: A table of the events, each with what emits it.
viewpoints.label: Event catalogue

viewpoints.description: The processes and their steps as Warnier–Orr diagrams: what each is made of, what repeats, what is an alternative and what runs at once.
viewpoints.label: Process (Warnier)

viewpoints.description: One process and its steps as a Warnier–Orr diagram: a view per process.
viewpoints.label: Process
